about: Written by hand: the workspace reorganized by one dependency-injection rule (Sam, msg 1938), with Sam's decisions on it (msgs 1939, 1952, 1978, 1979, 1981, 1984, 1986, 1987), as a transformation of the current map. propose.py applies it to map-data.js and writes proposed-data.js; it stops if a trait has no decision, or anything named here is not in the map. A chart for planning, not a change to the code. Every entry has a status: decided (by Sam) or recommended (pending Sam). Item 7, the kkt-config breakup in config-split.json, is part of the proposal, accepted by Sam (msg 1979).
rule: Every trait a crate depends on is a contract, and it is declared by its consumers, not by the crate that implements it.

If a contract is used by more than two crates, it lives in its own contract-only crate (traits, pure value types, and test doubles behind `testing`). Its real implementations move to separate implementation crates that only programs depend on. Model: kkt-db (contract) and kkt-db-sqlite (implementation).
If it is used by two crates or fewer, each consumer declares its own contract, and the program adapts the implementation to it.
Used by: crates other than the definer and the implementers that take the trait in a public slot or call through it, in normal dependencies. Test-only use is listed separately.

new_crates.name: kkt-db-sqlite-db

new_crates.name: kkt-backup-os
new_crates.concern: Writing and pruning backup folders on disk: `write` and `prune`, which the program calls. kkt-backup's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-shutdown-os
new_crates.concern: The operating system's stop signals: `StopSignals`, which the programs install and which stop kkt-shutdown's `Shutdown`. kkt-shutdown's `real` feature moves here.

kkt-clock::Clock.result: Shared contract: stays in kkt-clock, which becomes contract-only (Clock, Time, Span and the time text functions, FixedClock behind testing). SystemClock moves to kkt-clock-system as a plain type; each program adapts it to Clock (strict rule).

kkt-names::Entropy.result: Shared contract: a new contract crate kkt-entropy (Entropy; random_chars, which takes the alphabet as an argument; the test doubles). OsEntropy moves to kkt-entropy-os as a plain type; each program adapts it to Entropy (strict rule). kkt-names keeps handles, IDs, name packs and the operator and admin names, and depends on kkt-entropy. kkt-rules keeps its token alphabet private; kkt-admission and kkt-names pass their own character sets.

kkt-identity::Identify.result: Two consumers: kkt-mcp and kkt-server each declare their own Identify (with Identified and Identifying). kkt-server takes one value that meets both and gives that same value to /mcp, /mcp-admin and the web gate, so there is still one identity decision. kkt-identity becomes kkt-identity-keymode, an implementation crate holding KeyMode, which implements neither; each program adapts it once to both.

kkt-store::Reads.result: One consumer: kkt-rules declares Reads, with copies of the record and filter types it uses, and the check every store must pass (swarms_stay_apart). kkt-store implements nothing and keeps its own record types; each program adapts kkt-store's store to Reads and Writes, a large adapter (73 methods) that maps each record type. kkt-pro's store would be adapted the same way.

kkt-db::Backend.result: kkt-db keeps the contract. kkt-db-sqlite implements none of it; each program adapts SqlitePlace to Backend, Connection and Evolve, a large adapter (14 methods). This changes the model pair kkt-db and kkt-db-sqlite.

decided_items.text: random_chars moves to kkt-entropy and takes the alphabet as an argument. ALPHABET becomes private to kkt-rules, for both making and spotting tokens. kkt-admission and kkt-names pass their own character sets.

Operator and admin names stay in kkt-names. AdminName is split: its name rules stay in kkt-names; bound_to and bound_in (tying the name to the key's hash) move to kkt-admission. kkt-store's private OPERATOR copy goes, and kkt-store takes it from kkt-names.

The history from before kkt-db moves out of the program. kkt-store owns it as database-neutral facts (old 21 → core 1, 22 → core 2, the dropped handoff_note columns). kkt-db defines the neutral shape (today kkt-db-sqlite's Legacy). kkt-db-sqlite keeps only the SQLite part (user_version, the adoption). The program wires it and supplies the "upgrade with kkt 0.10 first" message.

kkt-store's testing offers an in-memory store on kkt-db's testing::MemoryPlace, and the fail-a-write hook. The tests of kkt-rules, kkt-identity-keymode, kkt-mcp, kkt-server and the fake product dev-depend on kkt-store only, not kkt-db or kkt-db-sqlite. kkt-store's own tests run on both backends. They wrap that store in kkt-store-rules' RulesStore (item 15).

kkt-agent-client stops depending on kkt-watch. It offers plain methods with its own types (channels, handle, latest ID, message, wait, the admin polling included). The program holds a thin adapter implementing kkt-watch's Server and mapping the failures.
Both Failure enums stay; the program's adapter maps one to the other.

kkt-config is broken up by domain, as proposed (accepted in msg 1979): format and fixed facts move into the crate that owns them, tuning values become settings fields the program fills, operator settings and defaults go to kkt-settings or the program, and kkt-config keeps only what is truly cross-domain. The table lists every item.
Under each type, the page lists the contracts it implements with their methods, then its own methods, in both the current and the proposed map.

The strict rule covers only another crate's contract. A crate may implement its own traits: FixedClock implements Clock, the entropy test doubles implement Entropy, kkt-db's own implementations and MemoryPlace's Evolve stay, DryRun implements System, and SameSource stays in kkt-web and implements Sources (msg 1984).

kkt-server's Parts::new and Parts.db, its record_run, and the fake product's Product::start take a store meeting kkt-rules' Reads and Writes. kkt-server no longer names kkt-store's Db, and uses kkt-rules' copies of the record types.
Each program wires the new Parts slots sources, gate and wording from its adapters over RulesSources, AdmissionGate and NoticeWording.
kkt-web's must-not: it depends on no rules, store, admission, identity or implementation crate; each program adapts what it passes in.
The preview example and the preview's tests move to kkt-web-preview, which has its own assembly and adapters. kkt-web's dev arrows to implementation crates go.

Construction order (msg 1984 item 7, accepted in msg 1987): Parts take a SourcesFactory and a GateFactory. The program passes functions that kkt-server calls with the rules and web sessions it builds; they return the adapted Sources and Gate. kkt-server keeps the construction, and the program keeps the adapting. The wording needs no factory: the program builds it first.

Shared adapters (msg 1984 item 8, accepted in msg 1987): an adapter that several programs and tests need lives in a small composition crate that depends on both sides, so neither side knows the other. kkt-store-rules adapts kkt-store to kkt-rules' Reads and Writes (73 methods); kkt-db-sqlite-db adapts kkt-db-sqlite to kkt-db's traits (14). The programs and the tests use those instead of copies of their own.

kkt-format is dissolved (msg 1986). Formatter and what goes with it become kkt-mcp-formatter, in Surfaces, kind logic. NoticeWording moves to kkt-names and takes plain input; kkt-rules still declares OperatorWording, and the program adapts.

Layers say where in the system a crate sits, in both maps: Programs, Assembly, Surfaces, Access, Core, Data, Operations, Clients, Foundations and Dev-only. Each implementation crate sits beside its domain; the shared adapter crates sit in Data (msg 1986).

Each crate has a kind, written by hand: contract, logic, effect, composition, configuration or test support, and in the current map mixed. Boxes are outlined in their kind's colour. The generator checks what it can and reports mismatches; in the proposed map a mixed crate is a violation (msg 1981).

No crate in the proposed map is mixed, compositions included (msg 1992): kkt-server's listen and Listening go to kkt-server-listen, kkt-backup's write and prune to kkt-backup-os, and kkt-shutdown's StopSignals to kkt-shutdown-os. Only the programs use them. LogPolicy is configuration: it goes to kkt-settings, so kkt-provenance records it without depending on kkt-logs (msg 1995). Tagged "follows from Sam's rule"; C7 is open.

not_traits.note: Concrete types, not traits, so the rule does not apply as written. Shutdown is taken by kkt-server's build and kkt-mcp's transport; StopSignals, the real signals behind `real`, is used only by programs.

conflicts.title: Real implementations behind `real`, or in implementation crates
conflicts.text: PRINCIPLES rule 8 and CLAUDE.md put what touches the machine in the crate that owns the area, behind its `real` feature, and the rule moves it to implementation crates.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam): each OS implementation moves to its own `*-os` crate as a plain type that implements nothing, and the consumer's `real` feature moves with it. The program writes one adapter per consumer trait: Host for kkt-container, kkt-remote-access and kkt-client-config, System, Prober and Disk.

conflicts.title: Reads and Writes: the store's contract, or the rules'
conflicts.text: Reads and Writes have one consumer, kkt-rules, so the rule has kkt-rules declare them. The plan has a second store (kkt-pro's) used through the same Reads and Writes, with the agreement test and the two-swarm test over those traits.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam): kkt-rules declares Reads and Writes and the record types they use; kkt-store implements nothing and keeps its own. Each program adapts kkt-store's store to them: a large adapter, 73 methods, mapping each record type. testing::swarms_stay_apart moves with the traits and runs over that adapter; kkt-pro's store would be adapted the same way. The adapter lives once, in kkt-store-rules, for the programs and the tests; swarms_stay_apart runs over it there (item 15).

conflicts.title: kkt-server's web adapters
conflicts.text: Step 6 made kkt-server's adapters to kkt-web's contract public, for a product that builds its own page; the rule would have the programs adapt them.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam): RulesSource, RulesSources and AdmissionGate stay public but implement nothing. Each program adapts them and passes the Source, Sources and Gate into kkt-server through new Parts slots, and kkt-server mounts the page with them. The adapters need the rules and web sessions that kkt-server builds from Parts. The slots take factories that kkt-server calls with them (item 14).

conflicts.title: Who adapts OperatorWording
conflicts.text: The rule says the program adapts; kkt-format's NoticeWording is wired into the rules by kkt-server, which is not a program.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam): the program adapts NoticeWording to OperatorWording and passes it into kkt-server through a new Parts slot; kkt-server hands it to the rules.

conflicts.title: The model's own traits fall below the threshold
conflicts.text: Counted by the rule, kkt-db's Backend and Evolve have no consumer besides kkt-db itself, and Connection one, so they would not get a contract crate.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam): kkt-db-sqlite stops implementing kkt-db's Backend, Connection and Evolve, and each program adapts SqlitePlace to them: a large adapter, 14 methods. This changes the model pair: kkt-db-sqlite no longer implements its contract crate's traits. The adapter lives once, in kkt-db-sqlite-db (item 15).

conflicts.title: axum outside the three crates CLAUDE.md allows
conflicts.text: CLAUDE.md: axum is the HTTP framework of kkt-web, kkt-mcp and kkt-server only, and its types do not leave those three. kkt-server-listen serves the App kkt-server builds, which holds an axum Router, so it needs axum and the Router.
conflicts.resolution: For Sam: either CLAUDE.md names kkt-server-listen as a fourth axum crate, or kkt-server keeps the serving loop and takes an already-bound socket from kkt-server-listen, which then holds only the bind. The map shows the split as the rule asks, with this open.

withdrawn.text: Identify (one identity decision, or one per consumer) is not a conflict (Sam, via sage-cardinal, msg 1939): a shared trait does not guarantee one decision; the wiring does. kkt-server takes one identify value, which meets both consumer-declared traits, and gives that same value to /mcp, /mcp-admin and the web gate; the program wires KeyMode once.

assumptions.text: SeededEntropy (repeatable randomness for the web preview and the fake product's differential test, never for tokens) counts as a test double, so it moves into kkt-entropy behind `testing`, not to an implementation crate.
kkt-service's DryRun wraps another System and only prints what it would do; it is the crate's own logic over its contract, not a real implementation, so it stays.
The program kkt counts as a consumer when its code names a trait (for example Box<dyn watch::Server>), as the definition says; kkt-watch::Server's one consumer is the program.

"The record types Reads and Writes use" is taken as the 36 public types of kkt-store that the two traits' methods name (32), or that appear inside those types (AgentLaneRecord, ChannelNoteRecord, LaneSourceRecord) or inside StoreResult (StoreError). ChannelKind, the 16 channel kinds the tests go through, appears in neither trait, so it stays in kkt-store.

kkt-rules no longer names kkt-store's Db: its Deps and CommandLine take a store meeting its Reads and Writes, which is the program's adapter over kkt-store's Db. How it opens a transaction on that store is left to the refactor.

doc_edits.doc: The server over the admin endpoint, `/mcp-admin`, for `kkt watch --admin`: every channel, closed and hidden ones included, through plain methods; the program adapts it to kkt-watch's `Server` (item 5).

How notices name the operator, from the admin key's name or none: "The operator", or "The operator (via <name>)". It takes plain input, so kkt-names knows nothing of kkt-rules' Audit; the program's adapter maps Audit to it and meets kkt-rules' OperatorWording.

status_legend: "Decided by Sam" covers the rule itself (msg 1938) and what follows from it, and Sam's rulings: msgs 1939 and 1952, the strict rule (msg 1978), and item 7, the kkt-config breakup, accepted as proposed (msg 1979); msg 1984's fixes and its items 7 and 8 (accepted in msg 1987); and the layers, kinds and kkt-format's dissolving (msgs 1981 and 1986). "Recommended, pending Sam" is what rests on an assumption, which leaves only the move that rests on A1. "Follows from Sam's rule" marks what the rule requires once its checks run, without a ruling of its own (msg 1992): the effects split out of kkt-server, kkt-backup and kkt-shutdown.

strict.text: No implementation implements another crate's contract; the program always adapts (Sam, msg 1978). A crate may implement its own traits: FixedClock implements Clock, the entropy test doubles implement Entropy, kkt-db's own implementations and MemoryPlace's Evolve stay, DryRun implements System, and SameSource implements Sources (msg 1984). Sam rejected the refinement of msg 1952, which let an implementation implement its one consumer's contract directly, because it leads to tight coupling.

new_slots.name: sources
new_slots.note: a SourcesFactory: kkt-server calls it with the rules it builds, and it returns the program's adapter over RulesSources, meeting kkt-web's Sources (C4, item 14)

new_slots.name: gate
new_slots.note: a GateFactory: kkt-server calls it with the identity and web admission it builds, and it returns the program's adapter over AdmissionGate, meeting kkt-web's Gate (C4, item 14)

new_slots.name: wording
new_slots.note: the notices' wording, from the program's adapter over NoticeWording, which kkt-server hands to the rules (C5). The program can build it first, so it needs no factory

renames.concern: Key mode's identity: `KeyMode`, a plain type that implements nothing; it decides who a caller is from the key that let it in and the avatar's token, and each program adapts it once to kkt-mcp's and kkt-server's `Identify`.

The MCP tools' results turned into text or JSON, within the response size cap: `Formatter`, `Format`, its `Settings` and `MIN_RESPONSE_BYTES`. It is what was left of kkt-format, which is dissolved; `NoticeWording` moved to kkt-names (msg 1986).

kkt-clock.concern: Time: the `Clock` contract, kkt's time types `Time` and `Span`, the time text functions, and `FixedClock` behind `testing`. Contract-only: its real clock is in kkt-clock-system. The only crate that uses chrono.

kkt-names.concern: Avatars' handles, channel IDs, the name packs, and the operator and admin names with their rules. It draws randomness through kkt-entropy's `Entropy`, with its own character sets.

kkt-store.concern: The core's data: a store over kkt-db, with its own methods and record types, and the core's tables as migrations and their history from before kkt-db. It implements no trait; kkt-store-rules adapts it to kkt-rules' `Reads` and `Writes`. Its SQLite tests use kkt-db-sqlite-db.

kkt-rules.concern: Every permission decision and every change, for agents and the operator, each in one swarm. It declares the store contract it uses, `Reads` and `Writes` with their record types, and the check every store must pass.

kkt-db-sqlite.concern: SQLite, the only crate that knows it: it opens a SQLite database, in a file or in memory, adopts a database from before kkt-db by SQLite's `user_version`, and copies one for backups. It implements none of kkt-db's traits; kkt-db-sqlite-db adapts it.

kkt-db.concern: The database contract, for any database: values, tables, keys and constraints; a narrow language of questions and changes (not SQL); transactions; search; migrations as additions; the shape of a database from before kkt-db; the traits a backend meets, and its own in-memory backend behind `testing`. kkt-db-sqlite meets them through an adapter.

kkt-server.concern: Assembling the server from its parts and running it: the rules, `/mcp`, `/mcp-admin` and the web page; recording each server run. Its parts take a store meeting kkt-rules' `Reads` and `Writes`, the identity, the web page's sources and gate, and the notices' wording, each adapted by the program; it names none of kkt-store's types. RulesSource, RulesSources and AdmissionGate stay public, implementing nothing. Binding the socket is in kkt-server-listen.

kkt-agent-client.concern: The shared MCP client for agent commands: avatar credentials, and reaching the server as an agent or admin through plain methods with its own types. It knows nothing of kkt-watch; the program adapts it.

kkt-mcp.concern: The agent and admin MCP tools, what the two share, their HTTP transport, and what agents are told about each tool. It declares the `Identify` it asks.

kashkeshet.concern: The `kkt` command and everything it does on a machine: its subcommands and the files and environment they read, the settings and config file, the setup record, key files, how a client reaches the server, and one module per command that takes plain inputs. It holds the adapters the strict rule needs: one per contract it fills with another crate's implementation, except the store and database adapters it takes from kkt-store-rules and kkt-db-sqlite-db.

kkt-keymode.concern: A second program that assembles key mode again from the shared crates with none of the `kkt` program's code, with its own adapters, as the strict rule has every program write, and the shared store and database adapters. The HTTP-only end-to-end tests run against it in CI. Dev-only, never released.

kkt-fake-product.concern: The shared crates assembled as a product other than kkt would assemble them, with two swarms and `FakeIdentify`, its own type meeting both consumers' `Identify`. It adapts the implementations it wires, as every program does, and takes the shared store and database adapters. Its tests check that nothing of one swarm reaches the other. Dev-only, never released.

kkt-admission.concern: Whether an HTTP caller is let in at all, and as which `Principal`: no key, which of the server's keys, or (for another program's `Identify` to judge) any bearer token. Also web sessions, the checks on the server's keys, and which admin name a key carries (`server_keys::bound_to`, `bound_in`).

kkt-container.concern: Running kkt in Docker: its Compose files, its folder, and the commands that set it up, start, back up, upgrade and stop it. It declares the `Host` it runs them through; the real one is in kkt-container-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-service.concern: Running kkt as a service under launchd or systemd, and the plan of what the service runs. It declares the `System` it works through, and keeps `DryRun`; the real one is in kkt-service-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-remote-access.concern: Sharing a service-mode server over the machine's existing Tailscale login. It declares the `Host` it works through; the real one is in kkt-remote-access-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-client-config.concern: MCP client configs and their file formats, so `kkt connect` can add kkt to a client. It declares the `Host` it works through; the real one is in kkt-client-config-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-diagnostics.concern: `kkt doctor`'s checks and their plan, and setup's wait for a new server. It declares the `Prober` it checks through; the real one is in kkt-diagnostics-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-lane-files.concern: Lanes as files: the `<lane>.md` format, reading and writing a folder of them, and the folder's git commit. It declares the `Disk` it works through; the real one is in kkt-lane-files-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-web.concern: The human's pages, through a contract of its own: `Gate` says who is viewing each request, `Sources` gives each viewer its `Source`, and every change is a checked form post. `SameSource`, its own `Sources` for a page with one view, and the page scenarios every source must pass (`testing`).
kkt-web.must_not: Depend on the rules, the store, admission or identity, or on an implementation crate: each program adapts what it passes in to kkt-web's contract.

kkt-events.concern: Notices of new messages, agents, channels and members, and of hidden agents and channels: one bus for the server, each notice heard only in its swarm, with a buffer per swarm kept only while it has a subscriber. The buffer's size is a setting the program fills (item 7).

kkt-watch.concern: `kkt watch`: waiting for an agent's new messages (or every channel's, as admin) and the line printed for each. The server, clock, saved place, output and its retry and wait timings are injected by the program (item 7).

kkt-backup.concern: Backup folders: their names, what goes in them and their file modes, and which to prune; the disk work is in kkt-backup-os.

kkt-shutdown.concern: The stop signal: `Shutdown`, whose clones share one signal. The operating system's signals are in kkt-shutdown-os.

rejected.text: An implementation may implement a consumer's contract directly when it exists to serve exactly one consumer (msg 1952). Sam rejected it (msg 1978) because it leads to tight coupling; the strict rule holds.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Flags give the address, the seed and the preview's settings; a non-loopback address needs an access key and names the hosts to answer to.

steps.title: Gate
steps.text: PreviewGate, with the access key or open, over the example's adapters to the system clock and the operating system's randomness; the example adapts it to kkt-web's Gate.

steps.title: World
steps.text: Preview simulates a swarm from SeededEntropy and the seed; the example adapts it to kkt-web's Source, and kkt-web's SameSource gives every viewer that one source.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: kkt-web's router serves the page until a stop signal.

wiring.note: the simulated world, repeatable from the seed (A1)

open_questions.text: kkt-rules' unit tests cannot wire RulesStore, because a unit test that depends on kkt-store-rules sees a second copy of kkt-rules. The rule tests that need a store would become integration tests, which CLAUDE.md does not foresee (it puts them in src/tests.rs).

as worded, the rule also covers smaller adapters that several programs repeat. These are RulesSource, RulesSources and AdmissionGate to kkt-web (28 methods, all three server programs), NoticeWording (1), SystemClock (2) and OsEntropy (1) in every program, and KeyMode (6, kkt and kkt-keymode). The preview's two adapters (27) are shared by its example and its tests. The map applies item 15 only to the two crates named.
